assessment_summary: The proof breaks down at step 0040. Prior to this step, the text introduces the case where $p=0$ or $q=0$ (step 0031) and states the definition and limit properties of the Hölder mean for exponent 0. However, it never actually proves the inequality $M_p \le M_q$ for these cases. Step 0040 then incorrectly asserts that 'It remains to resolve the inequality for p, q \in \R_{\ge 0}'. This statement is logically flawed for two reasons: 1) it falsely implies the zero cases have been resolved; and 2) it unjustifiably restricts the remaining cases to non-negative real numbers, which entirely ignores the cases where $p$ or $q$ are negative (a restriction that is also contradicted later in step 0052/0059 when $q < 0$ is evaluated). Therefore, step 0040 is the first invalid deduction.
